statement: He told the Muslims he had been shown their place of emigration, a land of date palms between two lava tracts; people then emigrated to Madinah, including most who had gone to Abyssinia.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked against Bukhari 3905 (narration of Aishah).

statement: In a dream he saw himself emigrating to a land of palms and thought it al-Yamamah or Hajar, but it was Yathrib.
Al-Bara: the first to arrive were Mus'ab and Ibn Umm Maktum, then Bilal, Sa'd and Ammar, then Umar with twenty Companions.
notes: Machine-checked. That al-Bara was a boy then is from the Seerah.

statement: The emigrants left quietly, abandoning homes and property, which Quraysh seized.
Abu Salamah's wife and son were held back by their clans; he went alone; Umm Salamah was separated from them for about a year.
notes: From Ibn Ishaq, narrated from Umm Salamah.

statement: Suhayb gave up his wealth to be allowed to leave; the Prophet said 'Suhayb has profited'.
notes: Recorded by al-Hakim and others; grading to be confirmed. Narrated with 'it is reported'.

statement: Abu Bakr prepared to emigrate; the Prophet told him to wait as he hoped for permission; Abu Bakr held back and fed two camels on samur leaves for four months.
Few believers remained in Makkah besides the Prophet, Abu Bakr, Ali and those detained.

notes: Paraphrase of meaning; verse text checked in the dataset.

statement: Quraysh met in Dar an-Nadwah, considered confinement, exile and killing, and chose to have a youth from each clan strike together so Banu Hashim could not retaliate.
notes: From Ibn Ishaq. The report of Satan attending as an old man of Najd is left out.
